analysis:
The PR adds require_supported_macos() to scripts/install.sh (head lines 447-464), invoked at line 592 immediately after select_provider_identity. It refuses a fresh install on macOS < 27. It continues when the OS version is unknown or non-numeric, or when $BIN_DIR/$CLI_NAME or $PROVIDER_CONFIG already exists. Tests were added in scripts/test-install-onboarding.py.

Security effect: this is a client-side installer gate that only narrows installs. It does not alter the bundle hash check, the codesign designated requirement, the staged-app verification, or the coordinator binding. It does not touch provider authorization, App Attest, or the legacy MDM path.

The gate is advisory and is not an enforcement point. The grandfathering signal (existing binary or config file) is locally controllable, but the operator already controls their own machine. Serving authorization remains coordinator-side, per TB-011/TB-002: a legacy provider on an old OS still needs a qualified App Attest grant for base rewards, and the installer text matches that policy. Bypassing the gate (an attacker pre-creating a file) gains nothing beyond what a manual install could do, since the coordinator enforces eligibility, which is outside the supplied evidence.

The unknown-version fail-open path (MACOS='?') only permits install. configure_device_verification already handles that case without downloading an MDM profile. No new attack surface, secret handling, or injection was found. $MACOS comes from sw_vers and is only echoed.

The test harness extracts functions from install.sh and runs them in a temp HOME. It is test-only. The test excerpt is truncated; it references DEV_RELEASE, which is presumably defined earlier in the file. Remaining integration question: whether the platform-served install.sh snapshot is updated byte-for-byte, which is outside this review.
